hook.text: If you recorded yourself reciting Juz' 'Amma today, which rule would you most expect to hear slip?
hook.a: Often madd lengths, ghunnah, or a makhraj like ض or ث. An audit finds the real gaps.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation (tartil)' (Al-Muzzammil 73:4). The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it' (Bukhari).

check.why: Laam is not a qalqalah letter; before ه it is said clearly.

practice.q: Name the rule in «ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ» (112:2) when stopping.
practice.a: ٱللَّهُ: heavy laam (starting); ٱلصَّمَدُ: sun letter ص, and qalqalah on د at the stop.
practice.model: I do: starting with ٱللَّهُ, the laam is heavy. ٱلصَّمَدُ: ص is a sun letter, so no laam is said. Stopping: صَّمَدْ: د with sukoon is a qalqalah letter, so it bounces strongly.

lessons.title: Waqf signs in the mushaf
lessons.bigQuestion: 'Let's eat, Grandma' and 'Let's eat Grandma': one comma changes everything. How could a stop change the meaning of an ayah?
objectives: To understand the six main stopping signs of the Madinah mushaf and stop and restart correctly when reciting
successCriteria: All: name the six waqf signs and what they mean
Most: stop and restart (ibtida') correctly at ۖ and ۚ
Some: explain why the sign at 36:76 is lazim
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: protecting the meaning of Allah's words

keywords.def: reciting each letter with its right and its rules

hook.text: 'Let's eat, Grandma' and 'Let's eat Grandma': one comma changes everything. How could a stop change the meaning of an ayah?
hook.a: Stopping in the wrong place can join or split meanings wrongly; the waqf signs protect the meaning.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation (tartil)' (Al-Muzzammil 73:4). Knowing where to stop is part of tartil; the scholars of recitation placed small signs in the mushaf so readers stop where the meaning is complete.

starter.q: Recite Al-Mulk 67:2 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: The six signs
teach.note: Bismillah. These are the signs of the Madinah mushaf, written small above the line.

head: Sign
Name
Meaning
Example
rows: Must stop: joining would change the meaning
Stop at one of the two, not both

teach.heading: Why 36:76 is lazim
bullets: Joining would make 'We know ...' sound like their words
teach.note: The stop separates their speech from Allah's statement.

teach.heading: Stopping and restarting
bullets: Stop on a sukoon (tanween fathah becomes aa)
Never restart in the middle of a phrase
teach.note: Ibtida' (ابتداء): starting again. Model 67:3 stopping at ۖ, then starting at مَّا تَرَىٰ.

misconception.wrong: Stopping at ۙ (la) because you ran out of breath
misconception.right: Breathe earlier; at ۙ continue, or go back and restart

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: ۘ is waqf lazim: joining would give a wrong meaning.

practice.q: Read 2:2 «ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبُ لَا رَيْبَ ۛ فِيهِ ۛ هُدًۭى» and show the two allowed stops.
practice.a: Stop after رَيْبَ (then فِيهِ هُدًى joins), or after فِيهِ; never at both (mu'anaqah).
practice.model: I do: way 1: ... لَا رَيْبَ (stop), فِيهِ هُدًۭى لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ. Way 2: ... لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ (stop), هُدًۭى لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ. Not both.

practice.q: ۖ (صلى) means ...

independent.q: Waqf hunt (pupil PDF): find three ۖ and two ۚ in Al-Mulk and say what you would do at each. Today's rota group recites Juz' Tabarak placement surahs.
independent.model: The teacher finds 67:2 ...عَمَلًۭا ۚ: either stop (عَمَلَا) or continue (idgham into وَهُوَ).

independent.q: Extend: write the six signs with their meanings from memory.
independent.a: ۘ lazim; ۙ la; ۚ ja'iz; ۖ continuing better; ۗ stopping better; ۛ mu'anaqah.

independent.q: Stretch: explain how a wrong stop could change a meaning, using 36:76.
independent.a: Joining قَوْلُهُمْ إِنَّا نَعْلَمُ could suggest 'We know' is the disbelievers' saying.

exit.q: ۗ (قلى) means ...
Back to our ponder: 'Let's eat, Grandma' and 'Let's eat Grandma': one comma changes everything. How could a stop change the meaning of an ayah?
exit.a: Stopping in the wrong place can join or split meanings wrongly; the waqf signs protect the meaning.

lessons.title: Ayat al-Kursi: reading and rules
objectives: Recite Ayat al-Kursi (2:255) accurately
Identify rules in each phrase
Stop and start in sensible places

keywords.def: the Self-Sustaining, who sustains all things

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
What is the rule for noon before dhal?

teach.heading: Listen and recite
teach.note: Recite the opening: ٱللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ. Pupils echo phrase by phrase. This is a single long ayah in Surat Al-Baqarah, number 255. Many pupils know it already; focus on precision.

teach.heading: Phrase 1: rules
bullets: La ta'khudhuhu sinatun: silah sughra on hu
Sinatun wa la nawm: idghaam with ghunnah
teach.note: لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ: the haa between damma and sin gets silah sughra. سِنَةٌ وَلَا: tanween then waw, merge with ghunnah. نَوْمٌ لَّهُ: tanween then lam, merge without ghunnah. Ask pupils to say why each is different.

teach.heading: Phrase 2: rules
bullets: man dha: noon before dhal, ikhfa
teach.note: مَن ذَا: dhal is an ikhfa letter, so ikhfa. عِندَهُ إِلَّا: haa followed by hamzat qat', so silah kubra. بِإِذْنِهِ يَعْلَمُ: haa after kasra then yaa voweled, silah sughra. Misconception: pupils think dhal is an idghaam letter.

teach.heading: Phrase 3: rules
teach.note: بِشَيْءٍ مِّنْ: tanween then meem, idghaam bi-ghunnah. مِنْ عِلْمِهِ: noon sakinah before 'ayn, izhar. عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا: haa after kasra then hamzat qat', silah kubra. بِمَا شَاءَ: madd muttasil, 4-5 counts.

teach.heading: Last phrases
bullets: wa la ya'uduhu hifzuhuma: silah sughra
teach.note: كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ: the haa is followed by hamzat wasl, so no silah. This is a common error to correct. يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا: haa between two vowels, silah sughra. On stopping at الْعَظِيمُ, madd 'arid 2, 4 or 6, keep consistent.

practice: What rule applies to مَن ذَا?
Is there silah in كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ? Explain.
Which madd is in شَاءَ and how many counts?
independent: Recite the ayah in chunks, marking each rule
Record yourself and check against a model
Write the rule behind five words from the ayah
exit: Name one rule that gives silah kubra.
Why is there no silah in كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ?
lessons.homework: Learn Ayat al-Kursi securely and recite it to a family member.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and colour key for silah. Stretch: teach the silah rules to a partner with examples from the ayah.

lessons.title: Ayat al-Kursi: meaning and how tafsir works
objectives: Explain the main messages of Ayat al-Kursi
Describe the sources used in tafsir
Distinguish tafsir from personal reflection (tadabbur)

keywords.def: explanation of the meaning of the Qur'an by qualified scholars
reflecting on the Qur'an to apply its message

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.

teach.heading: The greatest ayah
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b
Which ayah is the greatest in the Book?
teach.note: This is reported in Sahih Muslim: the Prophet ﷺ asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b which ayah in the Book of Allah is the greatest, and Ubayy answered with Ayat al-Kursi. The Prophet ﷺ then struck his chest and prayed that knowledge would be easy for him. Keep the telling accurate and simple. Ask: why might this ayah be so central?

teach.heading: Phrase meanings (1)
bullets: No god but Allah, the Ever-Living, Self-Sustaining
Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him
To Him belongs all in the heavens and the earth
teach.note: Say each phrase slowly in English. Link al-Hayy to a life that never ends and al-Qayyum to the One who sustains everything. Ask: how is Allah's life different from ours? Reflect on dependence: we need rest; He does not.

teach.heading: Phrase meanings (2)
bullets: None can intercede except by His permission
He knows what is before and behind them
His knowledge is not encompassed except as He wills
teach.note: Intercession (shafa'ah) exists only by Allah's permission. Allah's knowledge covers everything; we know only what He lets us know. Misconception: shafa'ah does not belong to anyone independently. Ask: what does this teach us about humility?

teach.heading: Phrase meanings (3)
bullets: His Kursi extends over heavens and earth
Guarding them does not burden Him
He is the Most High, the Most Great
teach.note: Say that scholars have discussed what al-Kursi is; we accept what Allah has told us without trying to picture it. Ask: why does the ayah end with al-'Aliyy and al-'Azim? To remind us of Allah's greatness.

teach.heading: Tafsir and tadabbur
bullets: Tafsir uses the Qur'an and Sunnah
It also uses Companions' sayings and Arabic
Tadabbur is personal reflection after learning
teach.note: Teach the classical sources briefly: the Qur'an explains itself, the Sunnah, the understanding of the Companions, and Arabic language. Examples of well-known tafsir books: Tafsir al-Tabari, Tafsir Ibn Kathir. Quote 38:29: a blessed Book We have sent down so they may reflect on its ayat. Stress that tadabbur does not replace tafsir.

practice: Who may intercede, and on what condition?
independent: Write a one-line meaning for each phrase of Ayat al-Kursi
Draw a mind map of what the ayah teaches about Allah
Write a short tadabbur paragraph: how this ayah affects my day
exit: What is the difference between tafsir and tadabbur?
Which phrase of Ayat al-Kursi do you find most powerful?
lessons.homework: Write 120 words: what Ayat al-Kursi teaches about Allah and how it should shape my behaviour.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: phrase-by-phrase translation chart. Stretch: look up Ayat al-Kursi in a recognised tafsir and summarise one point.

lessons.title: Adab with the Qur'an
objectives: Describe the etiquette of reciting, listening and handling the Qur'an
Explain the reasons from the Qur'an
Make a personal adab plan

keywords.def: reciting slowly, clearly and with reflection
sincerity, doing something for Allah alone

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.

teach.heading: Before we recite
bullets: Make a sincere intention for Allah
Be in a clean, calm place
Seek refuge from Shaytan before reciting
teach.note: Cite 16:98: when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Discuss ikhlas: recite to please Allah, not to impress people. Ask: what can distract us when we recite?

teach.heading: Handling the mushaf
bullets: The majority of scholars say wudu to touch it
teach.note: Pupils should not place the mushaf on the floor or under other items. Many scholars rely on 56:78-79 for the view that wudu is needed to touch the mushaf; practice varies between madhhabs, so ask your teacher or imam for the position you follow. Reading from a phone or tablet is a question for scholars, do not give a ruling.

teach.heading: Reciting well
bullets: Do not rush; understand what you read
teach.note: Quote 73:4: and recite the Qur'an with measured recitation. Link this to Year 6 tarteel work. The Prophet ﷺ taught that the one who recites with difficulty has double reward (Bukhari and Muslim). Ask: how does this encourage those who find tajweed hard?

teach.heading: Listening
teach.note: Read 7:204: when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, that you may receive mercy. Discuss real situations: a recitation on the speaker, a recital in class, a prayer. Ask: how do we show adab when we are listening?

teach.heading: Living by it
teach.note: 47:24: do they not reflect on the Qur'an, or are there locks on their hearts? A hadith in Tirmidhi says that whoever recites a letter of the Book of Allah receives a good deed, and each good deed is multiplied by ten. Link adab to action: reciting is not the end, acting is.

practice: Which ayah tells us to listen in silence?
Name two ways to respect the mushaf.
independent: Make a two-column list: adab before, during and after recitation
Write a personal plan for five daily minutes with the Qur'an
Role-play listening to a recitation with proper adab
exit: Write one adab you will start this week.
Which ayah supports reflecting on the Qur'an?
lessons.homework: Follow your personal adab plan for five days and note how it feels.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: illustrated adab checklist. Stretch: research how one of the four madhhabs views handling the mushaf.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Mulk 67:1-4: reading and rules
objectives: Recite Al-Mulk ayat 1-4 accurately
Identify rules in each ayah
Use consistent stops and madd lengths
starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Which rule applies when noon sakinah meets qaf?

teach.heading: Listen and recite
bullets: We study the first four ayat
Echo the teacher in short phrases
teach.note: Recite ayah 1: تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ الْمُلْكُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ. Pupils echo. Explain that Al-Mulk has 30 ayat and we begin with the first four.

teach.heading: Ayah 1 rules
bullets: bi-yadihil-mulk: no silah, hamzat wasl follows
shay'in qadir: tanween before qaf, ikhfa
teach.note: بِيَدِهِ الْمُلْكُ: the haa is followed by the alif of al-, a hamzat wasl, so no silah. شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ: tanween before qaf is ikhfa. At the stop, the yaa is followed by a stop-sakin raa: madd 'arid. Ask pupils to say why the first haa is short.

teach.heading: Ayah 2 rules
teach.note: الْمَوْتَ وَالْحَيَاةَ: both lams are qamariyyah, since meem and haa are moon letters. Practise stopping on عَمَلًا: the tanween becomes an alif, 2 counts. Common error: pupils stop with tanween sound.

teach.heading: Ayah 3 rules
bullets: min tafawut: noon before taa, ikhfa
min futur: noon before faa, ikhfa
teach.note: مِن تَفَاوُتٍ: ta is an ikhfa letter. مِن فُطُورٍ: faa is an ikhfa letter. Ask pupils to list all ikhfa letters (15) and check both appear. تَرَىٰ: the alif maqsurah is madd tabi'i, 2 counts.

teach.heading: Ayah 4 rules
bullets: thumma irji'il-basar: join the hamzat wasl
khasi'an wa huwa: idghaam with ghunnah
teach.note: ثُمَّ ارْجِعِ الْبَصَرَ: when joining, we drop the hamzat wasl: thummarji'. يَنقَلِبْ: ikhfa before qaf. خَاسِئًا وَهُوَ: tanween then waw, idghaam bi-ghunnah. On stopping at حَسِيرٌ, madd 'arid. Peer-check each rule.

practice: Why is there no silah in بِيَدِهِ الْمُلْكُ?
Which rule applies to مِن تَفَاوُتٍ?
How do you read طِبَاقًا when stopping?
independent: Recite ayat 1-4 three times, marking each rule
Record and compare with a model recitation
Write the rule behind six words
exit: Name one ikhfa example in the passage.
Explain madd 'iwad with an example from the passage.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio, colour-coded rule key. Stretch: explain the stop rules to a partner without notes.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Mulk 67:1-4: meaning and memory plan
objectives: Explain the meaning of ayat 1-4
Reflect on purpose in life and death
Plan revision using a new-recent-old cycle

keywords.def: new lesson, recent revision, older revision

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.

teach.heading: Ayat 1-2: Sovereignty and purpose
bullets: Blessed is He in whose hand is all dominion
To test which of you is best in deeds
teach.note: Read 67:2 slowly. The word is ahsanu 'amalan, best in deeds, not most deeds. Ask: what makes a deed best? Sincerity and being correct are the usual answers given by scholars. Link to ikhlas from last lesson.

teach.heading: Ayat 3-4: Look again
bullets: You will not see any flaw in the Merciful's creation
Look again: your sight returns dazzled and weary
teach.note: Read 67:3-4. The surah invites us to observe: look again, and again, you will find no flaw. Ask: what in nature gives you awe? Bring in tafsir carefully: scholars explain 'khasi'an' as sight returning humbled and 'hasir' as exhausted.

teach.heading: Tadabbur questions
bullets: What is my test in life?
How do I respond to the beauty of creation?
teach.note: Pupils answer in pairs. Possible responses: study well, treat people kindly, thank Allah for creation. Remind them that the aim is to link meaning to action. Do not push controversial interpretations; rely on tafsir.

teach.heading: A revision system
bullets: Sabqi: the last few days' lines
teach.note: Introduce the three-part system used by many memorisers: sabaq (new), sabqi (recent), manzil (older). Pupils map their own surahs onto it: Al-Ma'un, At-Takathur, Al-'Asr, Al-Humazah, Al-Fil, Al-Mulk. Ask: how often should each be revised?

teach.heading: My plan
teach.note: Pupils write a two-week revision plan. Remind them that consistency beats long sessions. Share a few examples. Close with a dua to keep what we have learned.

practice: What is the meaning of ahsanu 'amalan?
Why does the surah tell us to look again?
What do sabaq, sabqi and manzil mean?
independent: Write the meaning of each ayah in your own words
exit: Which of your surahs is in sabqi this week?
lessons.homework: Follow your revision plan and tick off each day.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: translation chart with key words and a visual plan template. Stretch: compare 67:2 with another ayah on trials.

lessons.title: Recital assessment and reflection
objectives: Recite Ayat al-Kursi or Al-Mulk 67:1-4 with accuracy
Self-assess and peer-assess with the rubric
Set targets for the next half term

keywords.def: a set of criteria for judging quality

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and the basmalah.
Which passage will you recite and why?

teach.heading: Prepare
bullets: Make wudu if possible and take a calm breath
teach.note: Give pupils five minutes to prepare. Remind them of adab from last week: sincere intention, calm place, a short dua. Reduce nerves with encouragement.

teach.heading: Rubric
teach.note: Share the rubric with levels. Pupils recite individually or in breakout pairs. Use the rubric to mark accuracy and consistency. Stress that feedback is one strength, one target, one action.

teach.heading: Recite and give feedback
teach.note: Pupils recite and listen in turn. Use sentence stems: 'One strength was...', 'One target is...'. Keep the atmosphere supportive. Praise improvements since the audit.

teach.heading: Look back
teach.note: Pupils return to their audit grid from Lesson 1 and tick progress. Share a few successes aloud. Discuss strategies for the remaining rules.

teach.heading: Reflect
teach.note: Pupils write a short reflection and three targets. Close with a dua for sincerity and steadfastness with the Qur'an.

practice: Which rule is most secure for you?
independent: Recite your chosen passage for assessment
Complete peer feedback with the rubric
Write a reflection and three targets
lessons.homework: Practise your targets daily and record a new recitation next week.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: simplified rubric with sentence stems. Stretch: coach a partner on one rule.

lessons.title: Juz' 'Amma in six blocks: the revision rota
lessons.bigQuestion: 37 surahs and only 10 to 15 minutes a day. How would you divide them so none is forgotten?
objectives: To understand how to keep Juz' 'Amma secure with a six-block revision rota while new hifdh continues
successCriteria: All: recite one block with no more than three prompts
Most: keep a daily log for the week
Some: link the last ayah of one surah to the first of the next
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: steady, small daily deeds are loved by Allah

keywords.def: older memorised portion on a rota

hook.text: 37 surahs and only 10 to 15 minutes a day. How would you divide them so none is forgotten?
hook.a: Six blocks, one a day, so the whole juz' is revised each week.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Keep refreshing your knowledge of the Qur'an, for it escapes faster than camels from their hobbles' (Bukhari and Muslim).

starter.q: Recite Al-Ikhlas 112:2 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

hook.text: Ya-Sin begins with two letters, then an oath by 'the wise Qur'an'. Why might Allah swear by the Qur'an itself?

lessons.bigQuestion: Some surahs open with letters like الٓمٓ, يسٓ, قٓ. Nobody reads them as words. How are they read?

hook.text: Some surahs open with letters like الٓمٓ, يسٓ, قٓ. Nobody reads them as words. How are they read?
hook.a: By their letter names: yaa, seen; each name follows madd rules (2 or 6 counts).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance' (Al-Qamar 54:17). The meanings of these letters are known to Allah; we read them as the Prophet ﷺ taught.

teach.heading: Reading the opening letters
teach.note: Bismillah. Letter names of two letters (like يا) get 2 counts; three-letter names with a middle madd and a sakin last letter (like سين) get 6.

teach.heading: A Hafs detail: يسٓ وَٱلْقُرْءَانِ
bullets: In Hafs: izhar, a clear noon

practice.model: I do: يسٓ: yaa (2) seeeen (6), clear noon, then وَٱلْقُرْءَانِ: the alif after the hamza is badal, 2. Stop on ٱلْحَكِيمْ: 'arid, I choose 4.

independent.q: Stretch: why is the alif in «ٱلْقُرْءَانِ» only 2 counts though a hamza is near?
independent.a: The hamza comes before the madd letter (madd badal), not after it, so it stays 2.

hook.text: 36:7 says the word has come true for most of them, so they will not believe. What makes a heart refuse guidance?
hook.a: Heedlessness and arrogance; 36:6 describes a people heedless, never warned before.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: '[This is] a revelation of the Exalted in Might, the Merciful, that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are unaware' (Ya-Sin 36:5 to 6).

practice.q: Read 36:6 «لِتُنذِرَ قَوْمًۭا مَّآ أُنذِرَ ءَابَآؤُهُمْ فَهُمْ غَٰفِلُونَ» naming each rule.
practice.a: لِتُنذِرَ ikhfa; قَوْمًۭا مَّآ idgham; مَّآ أُنذِرَ munfasil and ikhfa; ءَابَآؤُهُمْ muttasil; فَهُمْ غَٰفِلُونَ izhar shafawi.
practice.model: I do: لِتُنذِرَ: noon before ذ, ikhfa. قَوْمًۭا مَّآ: idgham. مَّآ أُنذِرَ: munfasil 4, then ikhfa. ءَابَآؤُهُمْ: muttasil 4. فَهُمْ غَٰفِلُونَ: meem before غ, clear.

practice.q: «فَهُمْ غَٰفِلُونَ» is ...

independent.q: Breakout pairs: recite Juz' 'Amma block 2 (81 to 85) to a partner, then 36:1 to 8. Today's rota group recites 36:5 to 8 to the teacher.
independent.a: Partner rubric and target; teacher records rota scores.

independent.q: Extend: find an iqlab in Ya-Sin 36:9.
independent.a: مِنۢ بَيْنِ

independent.q: Stretch: explain why ikhfa before ق sounds heavier than before ذ.
independent.a: The ghunnah takes the heaviness of the following isti'la letter.

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Ya-Sin 36:6 has three ikhfa before the same letter. Which letter, and why might it be easy to get wrong?
exit.a: ذ: the tongue peeps out, so the ikhfa hum must prepare for it without pressing a noon.

lessons.send: SEND: rule card with letters in colour, the pupil PDF with examples spaced out, extra listening turn. EAL: key words with meanings beside the Arabic. Stretch: find and explain an example in a surah not on the slides.

lessons.title: Surat Ya-Sin 36:9-12: hear, understand and memorise
lessons.bigQuestion: 36:12 says Allah records what people send ahead and the traces they leave behind. What 'traces' could you leave?
objectives: To memorise Ya-Sin 36:9-12 accurately and recite it with its tajweed
successCriteria: All: recite 36:9-12 after the teacher, word for word
Most: recite 36:9-12 from memory with no more than one prompt
Some: link 36:9-12 to the ayat before and name the tajweed rules in them
lessons.smsc: Moral: leaving good traces that continue after us

hook.text: 36:12 says Allah records what people send ahead and the traces they leave behind. What 'traces' could you leave?
hook.a: Good deeds that continue after us: knowledge taught, charity, a good example (36:12).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they have put forth and what they left behind, and all things We have enumerated in a clear register' (Ya-Sin 36:12).

starter.q: Recite Ya-Sin 36:6 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: New ayat: Ya-Sin 36:9-12
bullets: Listen first: the teacher recites twice
Follow each word with your finger
teach.note: Begin with isti'adhah and Bismillah. Recite 36:9-12 slowly twice from the mushaf (spoken recitation only, no melody exercises), pointing to each word on the shared screen. The Arabic is the Qur'an in Uthmani script (Hafs 'an 'Asim, Madinah mushaf); check it against the school mushaf.

quote.text: وَجَعَلْنَا مِنۢ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّۭا وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّۭا فَأَغْشَيْنَٰهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ (٩) وَسَوَآءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ (١٠) إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلذِّكْرَ وَخَشِىَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ ۖ فَبَشِّرْهُ بِمَغْفِرَةٍۢ وَأَجْرٍۢ كَرِيمٍ (١١) إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُوا۟ وَءَاثَٰرَهُمْ ۚ وَكُلَّ شَىْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَٰهُ فِىٓ إِمَامٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ (١٢)

teach.heading: What the ayat mean
bullets: This is a translation of the meaning, not the Qur'an itself
teach.note: Read the English slowly. Remind pupils: only the Arabic is the Qur'an; any English is a translation of its meaning (here Saheeh International).

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them, so they do not see.
And it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe.
You can only warn one who follows the message and fears the Most Merciful unseen. So give him good tidings of forgiveness and noble reward.
Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they have put forth and what they left behind, and all things We have enumerated in a clear register.

teach.heading: Tajweed spotlight in today's ayat
teach.note: Point to each word in the mushaf. Pupils say the rule before you do.

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: mics in turn
teach.note: Talaqqi (تلقي): learning recitation by hearing it from the teacher. Work through 36:9-12 one ayah at a time. Keep a visible order of names (the register) so every pupil gets a turn across the week. Unmute only the pupils whose turn it is; everyone else whispers along with mics muted.
cycle: Pupils listen, mics muted, eyes on the words
Mics on in turn: three pupils repeat in register order
Teacher corrects one point for each
Whole class repeats softly, then moves to the next ayah

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

options: Whoever follows the reminder and fears the Most Merciful unseen
check.why: 36:11: 'You can only warn one who follows the message and fears the Most Merciful unseen'.

practice.q: Chunk and link Ya-Sin 36:9-12 together, ayah by ayah.
practice.a: The class recites 36:9-12 together without the mushaf.
practice.model: I do: chunk 36:9-12. Ayah 9: 3 times looking, 3 times without looking. Then ayah 10 the same way. Then link: recite 9 and 10 together twice. Finish by reciting the whole chunk once without the mushaf.

independent.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 36:9-12 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
independent.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.
independent.model: The teacher shows the 3-3-link method once: read the ayah 3 times looking, say it 3 times without looking, then link it to the ayah before it. Rota: names on screen, about 90 seconds each, so every pupil is heard at least once a week; the teacher marks the rubric and gives one target.

independent.q: In the portal box, list three 'traces' (36:12) you hope to leave.
independent.a: e.g. teaching someone a surah; sadaqah jariyah; a good example to siblings.

independent.q: Recite 36:1 to 12 and name one madd of each type you meet.
independent.a: Tabi'i, muttasil (ءَابَآؤُهُمْ, وَسَوَآءٌ), munfasil (مَّآ أُنذِرَ), 'arid (stops), lazim harfi (يسٓ).

exit.q: Ya-Sin 36:11: «إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ ...» Which word comes next?
Back to our ponder: 36:12 says Allah records what people send ahead and the traces they leave behind. What 'traces' could you leave?
exit.a: Good deeds that continue after us: knowledge taught, charity, a good example (36:12).

lessons.homework: Recite Ya-Sin 36:9-12 to a parent three times a day and revise Ya-Sin 36:1 to 8 and Juz' Tabarak (Al-Mulk); tick the portal revision log each day.
lessons.send: SEND: shorter chunks (one ayah), the pupil PDF with each word spaced, extra listening turn. EAL: key words with meanings beside the Arabic. Stretch: link to the next ayat and explain one rule to the class.

lessons.title: Madd and ghunnah in Ya-Sin 9 to 12; half-term recitation check
lessons.bigQuestion: Ramadan is coming: the month of the Qur'an. What will your daily Qur'an look like for four weeks?
objectives: To understand how madd and ghunnah shape Ya-Sin 1 to 12 and to show secure recitation against the rubric
successCriteria: All: recite Ya-Sin 36:1 to 12 with no more than three prompts
Most: keep madd lengths and ghunnah correct
Some: score 4 on every row and plan the Ramadan break
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: a Ramadan commitment to the Qur'an

hook.text: Ramadan is coming: the month of the Qur'an. What will your daily Qur'an look like for four weeks?
hook.a: Ya-Sin 1 to 24 (13 to 24 at home), the Juz' 'Amma rota and Al-Mulk: 10 to 15 minutes, logged.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'The month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was revealed, a guidance for the people' (Al-Baqarah 2:185).

starter.q: Recite Ya-Sin 36:9 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: Madd and ghunnah in 36:9 to 12
teach.note: Bismillah.

teach.heading: The half-term check
bullets: Plus your Juz' 'Amma block of the day
teach.note: One by one; pupils heard this week in the rota keep that score. Others revise in breakout pairs.

teach.heading: Break plan
bullets: Ya-Sin 13 to 24 at home (checked after the break)
teach.note: Plan's extension weeks: 36:13 to 24 are home hifdh, checked briefly after Ramadan.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

options: home hifdh over the break, checked after
check.why: In the founding year, weeks 4 to 6 of the unit are home hifdh, checked briefly and caught up later.

practice.q: Self-check: recite 36:9 to 12 and score each rubric row.
practice.model: I do: hifdh 4; makharij 4; rules 3 (iqlab in مِنۢ بَيْنِ: lips too hard); fluency 4. Target: light lips on iqlab.

practice.q: «إِنَّا نَحْنُ» (36:12) has ghunnah on ...

independent.q: Recitation check: recite 36:1 to 12 and your block to the teacher one by one. While waiting, write your break plan on the pupil PDF and revise in pairs.
independent.a: Rubric scores and one target per pupil in the portal.
independent.model: The teacher runs the first check as a model.

independent.q: Extend: plan which days you will learn 36:13 to 24.
independent.a: e.g. three ayat every two days.

independent.q: Stretch: read 36:13 to 16 with the mushaf and mark the rules.
independent.a: Annotated ayat.

exit.q: The Qur'an was revealed in ...
Back to our ponder: Ramadan is coming: the month of the Qur'an. What will your daily Qur'an look like for four weeks?
exit.a: Ya-Sin 1 to 24 (13 to 24 at home), the Juz' 'Amma rota and Al-Mulk: 10 to 15 minutes, logged.
